rules.statement: Do not change the signature (parameters, return type, nullability) of an existing public method; add a new overload instead.
rules.why: Shipped public surface is a contract consumers depend on, and changing a signature breaks them. Only additive changes are allowed without a major version bump.
rules.check: Diffs that modify parameters, return type or nullability of an existing public/protected member in place, rather than adding an overload.

rules.statement: Add new optional inputs to public types as nullable `init` properties, with the default resolved inside the library (fail-closed), never as new constructor parameters.
rules.why: A new constructor parameter is a binary-breaking signature change that breaks every call site and serializer. A nullable init property is additive.
rules.check: New parameters (even ones with defaults) added to existing public constructors for optional values, or optional init properties whose default the consumer is expected to supply.

rules.statement: Public configuration callbacks take a single growable options type (e.g. `Action<TOptions>`), and new settings are added as properties on that type rather than as additional callback parameters.
rules.why: A new bare callback parameter breaks every caller. An options type can grow additively.
rules.check: Public methods adding a new delegate/callback parameter or extra delegate arguments instead of extending the options type.

rules.statement: Append new members to public or serialized enums; never reorder or renumber existing members.
rules.why: Reordering or renumbering changes serialized and wire values.
rules.check: Enum diffs that insert members in the middle without explicit values, or change existing explicit values or order.

rules.statement: Remove shipped public API only across a major version: first mark it `[Obsolete("…", error: false)]` in a minor release and keep it working.
rules.why: Removing surface in a minor or patch release breaks consumers without warning.
rules.check: Deletions of shipped public types or members without a prior Obsolete stage or a major version bump, and Obsolete attributes with error: true added in a minor release.

rules.statement: Do not share a public type between two independently-versioned packages; keep it in a single owning package or duplicate it deliberately.
rules.why: A type used by two packages that can version apart creates a diamond dependency conflict.
rules.check: New public types placed in a shared package and consumed in the public surface of multiple independently-versioned packages.

rules.statement: Treat a nullability change on public surface (`string` ↔ `string?`) as a signature change that needs the same compatibility review as any other signature change.
rules.why: Nullability is part of the public signature and can break consumers.
rules.check: Diffs that toggle `?` on public parameters, returns or properties, and the matching changed lines in PublicAPI files.

rules.statement: Record every public API addition in `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`, and mark removals by prefixing the line with `*REMOVED*` there; never edit `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` outside a release.
rules.why: The Unshipped diff makes surface changes visible and intentional, and Shipped is the baseline the next release diffs against.
rules.check: PRs that change public surface without an intentional PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt diff, delete lines instead of marking them *REMOVED*, or modify Shipped.txt outside a release.

rules.statement: Bump the major version whenever a change removes public API or alters an existing public signature.
rules.why: After GA, only additive changes are compatible, so breaking changes need a major version.
rules.check: PRs with *REMOVED* entries or changed signature lines in PublicAPI files that don't include a major version bump.

rules.statement: In PublicAPI files, write interface type parameters without variance annotations, include `Type.Type() -> void` for non-positional readonly record structs but not for non-positional record classes, never list compiler-synthesized record members, and include the `extension(Receiver!)` block marker line for C# extension members.
rules.why: Wrong entries cause RS0016/RS0017 analyzer errors.
rules.check: PublicAPI.*.txt lines containing `<in ` or `<out `, record class parameterless ctor lines, synthesized Equals/ToString/etc. lines, or extension members missing their block marker.
